 ATP Finals Tennis Best Bets & Predictions for Tuesday, November 17
 Today’s ATP Finals picks, with matchup analysis and betting insights for Tuesday, November 17. 
 By Zachary Cohen - November 16, 2026 3998 
 X Facebook Email 
 Looking for the best bets for the ATP Finals on Tuesday, November 17? We break down the day’s matches, analyzing form, playing styles, and the odds to find our favorite picks for the action in Turin, Italy. Here’s what we’re betting on — and why.
 MORE: Check out Gill Alexander’s ATP Finals best bets on our Pro Picks page! 
 Rafael Jodar vs. Arthur Fils
 Fils won the first meeting, beating the Spaniard 3-6, 6-3, 6-2 in the Barcelona semifinals. That was on clay, though, and Jodar has had more head-to-head success on hard courts. The two have met twice since, and Jodar won both by the same scoreline, 7-6 (5), 6-3, in Washington and again in Montreal.
 Jodar should have some advantages here. His serve leaves a little to be desired, but these quicker conditions make him more dangerous with the ball on his racquet. He should rack up holds more easily than usual, and that’s a problem for Fils because Jodar is the much better returner. He owns the tour’s second-best break percentage (29.3%) over the last 52 weeks.
 Jodar also stands to benefit more from points that turn into extended rallies. He’s the more willing grinder of the two, and I’d argue Fils’ backhand is the shot most likely to break down.
 It’s also hard not to feel that Jodar looked better than Fils on the first day of round-robin play. Outside of Carlos Alcaraz, nobody in this field was beating Alexander Zverev the way he served on Sunday. Jodar still hung around and gave himself chances. Fils, meanwhile, wasn’t as impressive in a three-set loss to Ben Shelton, who lost focus for a moment in the second set and let the Frenchman extend the match.
 Bet: Jodar ML (-109) 
 Ben Shelton vs. Alexander Zverev
 This match is much tougher to call. Both players have the big weaponry these lightning-quick conditions demand. Over the last 52 weeks, Zverev is No. 2 on the ATP Tour in hold rate (90.3%) and Shelton is No. 3 (90.1%). Both are also top-five servers in tracked hard-court matches by TennisViz’s Serve Quality numbers.
 Given how they serve, expect long, competitive sets. Sets won also matter for tiebreaker scenarios within each group, so whoever drops the first set will be highly motivated to win the second.
 With no strong lean in either direction, I’m playing the Over on 2.5 sets as a half-unit play. It should be a fun way to sweat out the second match of the day.
 Bet: Over 2.5 Sets (+123 – 0.5 units)

 I usually have A LOT MORE on the Pro Picks page . These plays count towards my record and have been a big part of my success this season. Make sure you check them out. I’ll probably add a few more over there, so refresh that page throughout the day if you’re looking for action. That’s also where I put my Challenger-level plays, as well as picks for lower level ATP and WTA events.
